text:
maria: Heads up — after last night's kernel-selection tweak I'm seeing a small but sustained bump in soft 429s on prod. p95 token latency climbed and our admit window seems to be rejecting more short requests. logs attached below, wondering if this is admission logic or kernel performance interaction.

maria: snippet from prod logs:```2026-03-16T03:12:04Z INFO admit: soft_reject model=redwood-7b variant=q4_0 reason=queue_depth target_token_budget=800 actual_budget=600 decision=soft_429
2026-03-16T03:12:04Z DEBUG kernel-select: chosen=matmul_v2 batch_size=8 expected_latency_ms=45 measured_latency_ms=78
2026-03-16T03:12:05Z METRIC p95_token_lat=210ms prev_baseline_p95=120ms 429_rate=2.4% baseline_429=0.3%```

aj: I saw the same on canary. Kernel selector started preferring matmul_v2 for small micro-batches after the patch because we biased on avg_throughput. That kernel has worse cold-start for KV-cache hits (higher L2 thrash).

sam: cc @aj — suspect also quantized GEMM path mismatch. For sequences <32 tokens the qGEMM fallback does extra packing causing ~25–40ms overhead. Combined with slightly tighter token budgets we get more soft rejects.

lauren: Proposal: loosen per-request token_budget target by +20% for the next 6h and push a config flip that delays soft-429 until KV cache warm (>50% hit rate). Run canary traffic to 10% and measure p95/429.

devon: Bench run results from earlier this morning (bench-bot posted): p95 went from 120ms -> 200ms, 429 from 0.28% -> 2.1% after kernel change. Full table:```variant matmul_v1 matmul_v2
batch=1 p95 110 145
batch=8 p95 130 210
kv_hit_rate 0.62 0.36
```Seems matmul_v2 hurts KV-heavy workloads.

bench-bot: Automated note: perf-benchmark/1842099000 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1842099000/matmul_v2_ablation.csv

aj: Two orthogonal short fixes: 1) revert kernel preference biasing for small batches (force matmul_v1 for batch<=8 until we fix packing), 2) implement soft-429 grace window: if recent kv_hit_rate < 0.5, expand token_budget by factor f(kv_hit_rate). Pseudo:```budget = base_budget * (1 + max(0, 0.5 - kv_hit_rate))```

sam: Agree. Also add micro-benchmark that simulates KV-warm transitions: start cold, feed prefix-heavy traffic, measure kernel latency for first 1000 requests. If we can reproduce, we can iterate kernel tuners.

lauren: Operational checklist: - flip per-model budget +20% (6h) - enable delayed soft-429 (canary 10%) - revert kernel bias for small batches on canary nodes - collect p50/p95/p99 and 429_rate by model and region - rollback plan if 429_rate > 5% or p95 > baseline * 1.8

devon: I'll schedule the canary and add dashboards. Quick note: be careful with autoscaler thresholds — if budget expands too much we might oscillate capacity. Suggest coupling budget change with a short-term scaling cooldown.

maria: Thanks all. I'll own the config flip and coordinate with infra to revert the kernel bias on canary. Will post another update once we have the first 2h of canary data. :thumbsup:

aj: If anyone wants the micro-bench script I used locally:```# run microbench for batch sizes 1..16
for b in 1 2 4 8 12 16; do ./bench --model redwood-7b --kernel-selector=matmul_v2 --batch=$b --prefix-warm=0 --requests=2000; done```

sam: Thanks — will add qGEMM packing telemetry. Also filing a perf regression issue so we don't lose this: https://phab.redwood.com/T12345

lauren: tagging on-call @devon for scheduling and @aj for kernel revert when ready.

maria: update: canary started at 03:40Z, first 30m looks promising — p95 back down to ~130ms, 429_rate 0.4%. More to follow.
